subject: How to enable user to save instances of a reactive object for later use?

messages.author: 377eaa42ea5ffea2
messages.subject: How to enable user to save instances of a reactive object for later use?
parts:
In my shiny app I'd like to provide users with the option of saving the results of a simulation model (which is a data frame) that is dependent on a couple of inputs. The idea is to enable users to save different simulations using an action button (in the code below it is input$saveModel), have those saved simulations appear in a selectInput ui widget and then allow the users to select one or more of those saved models so that the results can be compared on a plot. The way I would like to implement this is to "stack" the data frames corresponding to all of the saved models using rbind and then filter the data frame based on the selected values in the ui widget. 

Where I am running into trouble is isolating and stacking the saved models. Below is the code I have in server.R 

#The results of the simulation stored as a data frame:

  prPov.df() <- reactive({ a function of user inputs })

  # The name of model that will be saved: 

  currentModel <- reactive({ paste("Model", input$saveModel, sep="_") })
  
 # Isolating the results for future use:

  isolate({ 
    x <- prPov.df()
    x$Model <- currentModel()
    assign(currentModel(), x) 
    .e <- environment() 
    })
 
#Stacking the results dataframe together to "accumulate" the saved results in one object

  modelsCompare <- reactive({ 
    if (input$saveModel == 0) return(NULL) 
    do.call(rbind, lapply(paste("Model", 1:input$saveModel, sep='_'), get, as.environment(.e))) 
    })

My thought is that if the user clicks the action button three times (but before clicking, toggling the inputs to get different results), three data frame objects will be saved: "Model_1", "Model_2" and "Model_3". However when I run this, the console gives me an error message saying that it cannot find the object "Model_1". 

As an R and shiny newbie, any support is very much appreciated. 

Kind regards, 

Paul
